text:
You've got the first part exactly right! An object in motion will stay in motion.

But you've hit on a really common misconception with the second part. A force isn't needed to *keep* an object moving. An object in motion will coast at a constant velocity all on its own, forever, as long as no forces act on it.

The key is that a force *changes* an object's motion — it makes it speed up, slow down, or change direction.

Here's a question: if you slide a book across a table, it slows down and stops. Why does that happen, according to Newton's First Law?

updates.reason: Misconception about the role of force.
